# Welcome

Welcome to the online site for Geog4/6300: Data Science in Geography. This course is offered each fall within the University of Georgia's Department of Geography. It provides a review/introduction to both geostatistical analysis and to using a code-based approach (specifically using R) for doing quantitative research. 

This course is NOT a GIS class, but we will cover how to load and work with spatial data and use elements of spatial analysis. It spends more time on data cleaning and manipulation that most GIS coursework as well as reviewing statistical techniques such as tests of difference and regression modeling.

::: {.required-actions}
# Before you start 

Download and install the following

- [The R software package](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/){target="_blank"}
- [The RStudio IDE](https://posit.co/downloads){target="_blank"}
- [Git](https://git-scm.com/install/){target="_blank"} (not required but recommended)
- [Github Desktop](https://desktop.github.com/download/){target="_blank"} (not required but recommended)

You should also create [an account on Github](https://www.github.com){target="_blank"} if you don't already have one.
::: 

# Course objectives and learning standards

The main objectives of the course are as follows:

  1. Understand basic concepts and methods of data collection and description
  2. Understand basic concepts of mathematical probability theory
  3. Understand the logic and practice of simple inferential statistics
  4. Understand correlation and regression analysis
  5. Ability to use appropriate statistical techniques in tackling geographical problems.
  6. Ability to comprehend academic literature that uses statistical techniques.

A more detailed list of skills that students will demonstrate through their coursework is available [on this learning standards page](learning_standards.qmd).
